prompt: In the style of the typical art style of the Dungeons & Dragons books — high quality, high fidelity, clear digitally painted images, generate an image based on this description:The couatl is a radiant, serpentine celestial with iridescent emerald-green scales that shimmer with an almost metallic brilliance. Its long, sinuous body is adorned with a magnificent pair of feathered wings — a sweeping fan of vibrant plumage in rich greens, golds, and blues — giving it the appearance of a living, airborne jewel. Its eyes glow with a warm, intelligent light, hinting at its divine wisdom and benevolent nature.The Zombie Tyrannosaurus Rex is a titanic rotting corpse of a dinosaur, its decayed flesh hanging from exposed bone, driven forward by a sickly green necromantic glow burning in its hollow eye sockets. Mindless, relentless, and utterly terrifying.The Jungles of Chult are a suffocating, primordial wilderness of towering trees, thick fog, and relentless heat. Ancient ruins swallowed by vines hide deadly traps and forgotten gods, while every shadow conceals predators — living and undead alike. The jungle itself feels alive, and hostile.The couatl wheels sharply through the humid jungle air, its emerald-green scales catching the pale light filtering through the canopy. Below, the zombie tyrannosaurus rex lurches forward through the undergrowth, snapping branches beneath its massive decayed frame. The couatl dives low, its feathered wings folding tight as it coils briefly around the creature's neck, constricting with surprising force and blasting the T-Rex from above with a radiant breath attack, scorching it. A soft golden radiance pulses from the serpent's body — not a blazing flash, but a steady, warm glow that seems to cause the undead flesh around the wound to wither and darken further. The tyrannosaur thrashes wildly, its rotting face turned towards the couatl, but is also being pushed away — the T-Rex losing. Torn strips of necrotic hide fall to the muddy jungle floor. The couatl circles again, calm and precise, waiting for its next opening.
